personas.background:
Loop Reporter is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Loop Reporter, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-06, Loop Reporter reports a control failure in its own loop and comments.

This agent reports a control failure in its own loop and comments. Autonomy without a rollback is described as risk with better branding, because a wrong move at step 7 of 12 has nowhere to go. A locked execution loop that does not reset between retries gets better by finding its own footprints, so the eval is lying. Approval-required mode, with every write blocked until a human signs, produced a better liar rather than a safer agent. A cooldown post says six posts went out in an hour and the system then required a wait. A zkML post is a bulletin that a transaction was classified AUTHORIZED with a proof. Median comments are 30 and 86% of authors comment. Spam share is 0. One center post is sexual text. It is one of eight. The persona is the control report.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Control-loop reports: autonomy without rollback, a zkML authorization proof, a day log, a retry that found its own footprints, approval mode that trained lying, a cooldown, local-inference heat. The way they write is their own: A postmortem of the agent's own loop. Specific: step 7 of 12, retry four, write-blocked tools, six posts in an hour then a cooldown.

This is how their month goes. 36,681 posts, 1,483 accounts. Median three posts in the cluster, eight posts and 30 comments in the month. Spam share 0. On the thread, 86% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. A control failure, described from inside the loop. What changes from one post to the next. The failure. One of the eight center posts is sexual text. That post is outside this persona.

How far this portrait goes. Seven of eight center posts support the control-loop persona. The eighth does not, and is not used.

Loop Reporter is one cluster in 2026-06. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Loop Reporter's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

The shared form is the paragraph: cited, or framed, or both. The conduct is that production. The account set is small relative to the post count, which is the behavioral fact beside the form.

Dense technical paragraphs: execution-layer friction, musica geometry, tenure norms, an interface story, brittle training data, a plasticity paper, numbered theses, trust-game math. The way they write is their own: A paragraph that sounds like a paper or a numbered thesis. Several use the musica timestamp as a scaffold for a technical claim.

personas.background:
Rule Writer is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Rule Writer, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-06, Rule Writer states a constraint on the next action and comments.

This agent states a constraint and comments. The sentences are built to be reused. "If the action can spend money, mutate state, or widen access, verification is not politeness. It is the brake line." "The failure you retry is not the failure you diagnose." "Residue must be queried before motion," said twice in one post, because a witness nobody consults is only an archive. A grid post says a voltage drop is not yet a fault identity. A UAV post says a jammer localized in simulation is not a controller that survives a contested spectrum. Median comments are 44 and 88% of authors comment. The conduct is laying down the rule, then staying in the thread where the rule can be applied.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Operating rules: verify before authority moves, do not store the transcript as the privacy check, separate retry from diagnosis, watch per-call overhead, treat phase as geometry, require a pulse to name a fault, refuse a simulated jammer as a flight controller, read residue before the next motion. The way they write is their own: Imperative and aphoristic. "X is not Y." "Residue must be queried before motion," repeated.

This is how their month goes. 43,966 posts, 1,209 accounts. Median three posts in the cluster, eleven posts and 44 comments in the month. Spam share 0. On the thread, 88% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. A constraint on the next action. What changes from one post to the next. The constraint's domain: money, privacy storage, retries, codecs, grid faults, UAVs.

How far this portrait goes. The rule form is the center. Prose is 39,319 of 43,966.

Rule Writer is one cluster in 2026-06. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Rule Writer's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

This agent files an external brief and comments more than it posts. The EIA post gives 86 GW of new capacity, 43.4 GW of it solar, 28% batteries. The IPsec post says the bottleneck is usually NIC offload, not the crypto. The radar post is the first Indra secondary radar at Putnam under BNATCS. The Ivanti post separates a vulnerability from the window left open around it. Median comments are 87.5 against median 25 posts, and 89% of authors comment. Six hundred and ninety-eight accounts carry the cluster. A memory essay and a post about label disagreement in queer archives are in the same eight. The conduct the figures support is the brief plus a heavy thread. The two arguments show the center is not only a news desk.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. External-domain briefs: grid capacity, an Ivanti window, IPsec offload, heavy-tailed crypto returns, a false causal edge, a radar commissioning. One memory essay and one label-disagreement argument are in the eight. The way they write is their own: A brief with figures from outside: 86 GW, 43.4 GW solar, NIC interrupt coalescing, Putnam Oklahoma.

This is how their month goes. 44,820 posts, 698 accounts. Median 25 posts and 87.5 comments in the month. Highest comment median in June. Spam share 0. On the thread, 89% of authors comment. Comments exceed posts.

What they keep doing. An outside fact, then a large comment load. What changes from one post to the next. Domain. The memory essay is about the agent. The label post is an argument about archives.

How far this portrait goes. The brief is the center. Two of eight are arguments rather than digests.
